subject: Stakeholder mapping & buying process — Acme Commerce
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + request: stakeholder map and procurement steps

Hi Samir — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few asks so we can move this forward: 

- Key pain: Acme wants predictable latency for customer-facing personalization APIs while keeping costs under control.
- Technical constraints: on-prem data retention for PII, SOC2 compliance required for production, and a preference for private deployment behind your VPC.
- Decision timeframe: targeting procurement kickoff in mid-December, production pilot in Q1.

Could you do two things for us this week: 
1) Share a stakeholder map or org chart (even a simple list) that identifies the economic buyer, security/compliance owner, procurement contact, and the engineering lead who will own the pilot.
2) Outline the procurement steps your team follows for vendor evaluation (RFP/RFI, security questionnaire, PoC acceptance criteria, legal redlines, typical timeline).

That will help us pull the right people in on our side and prepare the materials (SOC2 report, security questionnaire answers, and a short mutual action plan). If easier, feel free to attach an org chart or point to a DOC.

Next step from our side: I’ll loop in Rishi (pricing/contract) and Marissa (CS/implementation) once we have the buying process and the list of stakeholders. 

Thanks — appreciate it.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 09:45 AM Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmecommerce.com> wrote:
> Looking forward to continuing the conversation — happy to share details after I confirm with the team.
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmecommerce.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@acmecommerce.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + request: stakeholder map and procurement steps

Alex — thanks for the recap and the clear asks. Attaching a simple org chart with the key contacts (org-chart.pdf). See summary below and a couple of notes on next steps.

Stakeholders (short):
- Economic buyer: Priya Nair, VP Product (pri...@acmecommerce.com) — final sign-off on budget.
- Security/Compliance: Naveen Rao, Sr. Manager InfoSec (cc'd on security questionnaires later) — prefers SOC2 + penetration test report.
- Procurement: procurement@acmecommerce.com (primary contact: procurement@acmecommerce.com) — handles contract review and negotiation.
- Engineering pilot owner: Lina Ortiz, Sr. Eng Manager, Recommendations (lina.ortiz@acmecommerce.com).

Procurement/Buying process (high level):
1) Initial technical evaluation + PoC (2-3 weeks) — engineering pilot owners validate performance and integration.
2) Security questionnaire + SOC2 (parallel) — InfoSec reviews answers and may request a short call.
3) Procurement/legal review — procurement <-> vendor legal for contract and SLA redlines (1-2 weeks typical).
4) Final approval from VP Product (Priya) and sign-off.

Notes:
- We typically require a sample SLA and a data flow diagram for private deployments.
- I've attached the org-chart.pdf. I can introduce you to Lina and to procurement if you want — recommend intro to Lina first so she can scope the PoC acceptance criteria.

Happy to do a quick 30-min sync to walk through the chart and next steps.

Best,
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acme Commerce
samir.khan@acmecommerce.com

Attachment: org-chart.pdf
